model_and_version_evidence.primary_source_match: Wording and line order match the power-on screen illustrated on printed page 12 of the Commodore 64 User's Guide (Commodore Business Machines, Inc.; https://archive.org/details/commodore-64-user-guide/page/n27/mode/1up). See evidence/source-excerpts.md.
model_and_version_evidence.model_conclusion: The image names COMMODORE 64 and BASIC V2 and shows 38911 BASIC BYTES FREE, as the C64 manual does. It is a Commodore 64 screen, not a VIC-20 or other Commodore model. This rests on the image's text plus the manual, not on appearance.

measured_layout.text_grid: 8 x 8 cells aligned at (20,22); row 1 columns 4-34, row 3 columns 1-38, row 5 columns 0-5, cursor at column 0 row 6

authenticity_findings: Capture method is undocumented: the page says only 'Own work'.
Only two exact RGB values occur, so the image is a digital render (an emulator capture or an assembled image), not a photograph or video capture of real hardware.

The blue screen area is 320 x 203 px. A 25-row, 8-pixel text screen is 320 x 200, so the image has 3 extra blue lines at the bottom. This suggests cropping/editing or an inaccurate source rather than an unaltered hardware-exact frame. The text content and layout are unaffected.
Border and screen colours follow the stock C64 light-blue-on-blue power-on scheme; the exact RGB values are one palette interpretation, not measured hardware output.

transformations_for_editorial_frame.summary: Frame 1 (cursor visible) of source/original.gif, converted to RGB, scaled 3x with nearest-neighbour to 1080 x 744, centred at (420,168) on a black 1920 x 1080 canvas. No crop, no stretch, no retouching, no watermark removal (the file has none), no added text or UI. Reversible: crop (420,168,1500,912) and downscale 3x nearest to recover frame 1 exactly.
transformations_for_editorial_frame.frame_choice: Authored production choice: the cursor-visible frame shows the prompt waiting for input. Frame 0 differs only by the missing cursor block.
